headline: Anthropic raises $81.3 billion in the largest stock market listing on record
summary: Anthropic, the AI company that makes Claude, sold about 980 million shares at $83 each, raising $81.3 billion, the company said late on Wednesday 18 November. The shares are due to start trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.
why: It tops SpaceX’s roughly $75 billion listing in June. The first day of trading is a test of how much investors will pay for AI after weeks of swings in tech stocks.

event.t: Anthropic said it sold about 980 million shares, more than the 825 million it first planned, because demand far exceeded forecasts. The $83 price was above its $70 to $78 range.
Anthropic set the $70 to $78 range in a filing on 10 November.
Separately, large tech companies including Nvidia are investing a further $26 billion, bringing the total raised to about $107 billion.

updates.t: Anthropic confirmed late on Wednesday that it sold about 980 million shares at $83 each, raising $81.3 billion. That is more than the roughly $75 billion SpaceX raised in June, making it the largest stock market listing on record.
updates.why: It shows strong investor demand for AI despite weeks of swings in tech stocks.

updates.t: In Asia on Thursday, most stock markets closed lower despite the record listing. South Korea’s Kospi fell 1.26% and Taiwan’s main index 1.75%, while Japan’s Nikkei was almost flat. AFP said worries about Nvidia and further Fed rate rises weighed on trading.
